business: TradeCatch (a bilingual AI phone receptionist for Québec contractors)
by_segment: Small service business, 2 to 5 employees (business revenue)
Renovation, roofing or landscaping business (business revenue)
Solo contractor (plumber, electrician or HVAC), business revenue
by_behaviour: Personal phone, voicemail or an employee answers
why_not: Winter is crazy for us and I do lose callbacks, so the problem is real, but I'm not dropping two grand on setup for a robot I've never heard handle one of my customers. I'd call the demo line, maybe, but I wouldn't sign anything this week.

I'd call the demo line in both languages and probably book the call, but I don't hand over 2,000 $ before I've seen it work for a business like mine. There's no testimonial, no client name, no numbers on recovered jobs, nothing that tells me this has worked for anyone yet.

Losing that $9,000 kitchen job stung, but that quote sat because I didn't get back to him, not because nobody answered the phone. Two grand up front plus 249 a month, before I've seen it catch a single job, is a lot to bet when my notebook and texts mostly work.

Two thousand dollars just to get started, before I know if it catches even one job I'd have missed, is a lot to put down on a phone answering thing. The monthly I could live with, but I'm not paying the setup this month on a first look.

My whole schedule already lives in my CRM, and this only books into Google Calendar, so I'd be retyping leads on Sunday nights or running two systems. Two grand up front plus 249 to 349 a month for something that doesn't plug into what I use isn't a clear win yet.

Missed calls on a job do cost me work, and I'm glad I keep my number. But my appointments already live in my scheduling/CRM tool, and this only texts me or books into Google Calendar, so I'd end up retyping every lead on Sunday night. That's a second system, and I'd be paying $2,000 up front just to get it.
why_yes: I lost a $9,000 kitchen last month because nobody got back to the caller. If this saves one job like that a year, the setup and the monthly fee pay for themselves, so I'd sign up for Essential after I call the demo line and it sounds like a real person in proper Québec French.
flip: Calling the demo line myself, in French, as an angry customer with an urgent problem, and having it sound natural and text me the right details, plus being able to try it a month before paying the full setup fee.
